A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UPD research and retain the core benchmarks. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable, allowing additions, removals and relocated material to be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of seven VLMs, instruction-tuning experiments, ablations and human validation of automatic scoring.

after.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of 22 LMMs, additional prompting and diagnostic experiments, MMMU-AAD results and retained instruction-tuning experiments.

M1.justification: The UPD construction procedures, base/option/instruction prompts and A-OKVQA LoRA recipe remain substantively unchanged, including 10,000 samples and the 6:2:2 Standard:AAD:IVQD mixture. CoT and self-reflection are newly evaluated existing baselines; no revision of the proposed architecture, loss or tuning algorithm is established.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual expert-level evaluation on 459 MMMU-AAD questions in Appendix B.6/Table D; v1 only discusses expert-level extension as future work. V2 also evaluates an answer-supplied diagnostic scenario. The original 820 AAD, 919 IASD and 356 IVQD questions and A-OKVQA training coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands from seven to 22 models, retaining six and removing Qwen-VL-Chat. Additions include LLaVA-OneVision, InternVL2, Phi, Idefics, newer Qwen models and GPT-4o. V2 Table 3 also introduces evaluated CoT and self-reflection comparisons.

E3.justification: Automatic choice extraction changes from gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 to gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18. V2 adds OC-Dual evaluation, an answer-supplied diagnostic protocol and the filtered four-option MMMU-AAD evaluation. Circular evaluation and the original Standard/UPD/Dual metrics remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds language-versus-vision bottleneck diagnostics, an audit of GPT-4 filtering, OC-Dual-versus-Dual analysis, and detailed GPT-4o and open-versus-closed-model case studies. The existing training-mixture, data-size and cross-task transfer ablations are retained in Appendix D rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 adds Spearman rank-correlation reporting alongside r for OC-Dual versus Dual accuracy in Appendix E.1/Figure A; v1 reports r for Standard-versus-UPD/Dual relationships. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive model, CoT, self-reflection, MMMU and diagnostic results and revises retained scores. For example, GPT-4V AAD Base Dual accuracy changes from 49.0 to 52.4 in Table 1, with a changed automatic judge, so this is not an established same-protocol performance gain. Aggregate tuning results remain, but v1's detailed tuned-model Tables M–O are removed. V2 Table E also retains baseline values that disagree with its revised Table 1.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix E.1 introduces the mathematical definition of OC-Dual: success in Original Standard, Standard and UPD divided by success in Original Standard. The existing task definitions and Dual accuracy remain; neither version contains substantive theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: V2 reframes UPD as verifying robust or true understanding of MCQA and foregrounds weak Standard–UPD correlation, the open/closed-model gap and bottleneck-dependent prompting effectiveness. V1 instead prominently emphasizes prompt engineering and instruction tuning as solutions. These changes materially alter the headline scientific claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds model-specific language/vision explanations, distinguishes explicit refusal from merely supplying the missing answer, and warns that UPD tuning can impair general performance. It also explains how low Standard accuracy confounds expert-level evaluation and discusses why Dual remains preferable to OC-Dual.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents the MMBench snapshot, filtering audit, four-author curation with independent double review, A100 80GB hardware, and exact CoT/self-reflection procedures. Some v1 disclosures disappear, including the evaluator temperature, option-count augmentation explanation and spreadsheet-access link. The main repository link is retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the work around MCQA vulnerability and answer refusal, adding discussions of Wang et al. (2025), option-order robustness and knowledge-gap abstention. It explicitly acknowledges prior AAD work for LLMs and updates comparisons with recent multimodal models and unanswerable-question studies.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, the student anecdote is removed, and experiments are consolidated around numbered findings. General related work and instruction tuning move substantially into appendices, while terminology changes from VLM to LMM and the title and conclusion are revised.

P2.justification: V2 adopts two-column layout, transposes and expands the main comparison table, reorganizes radar charts, and adds bar charts, diagnostic plots and case-study displays. Detailed result tables reorder numerical ability columns without corresponding updates to their numbered headers, creating mismatches with Table A.

improvement.justification: Broader model evidence, bottleneck diagnostics, metric analysis and curation documentation strengthen v2. However, its detailed tables misalign ability labels with reordered values, undermining the central fine-grained diagnostic reporting. Its tuning table also retains unexplained baseline discrepancies: NeXT-13B IASD Base is 31.4 in Table E but 27.0 in Table 1. These material reporting problems coexist with substantial evidential gains, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
